premises.text: Existing EV cars are slow and expensive to market while developing-world two-wheelers are unsafe, impractical, and polluting
premises.evidence_span: these take forever to get to market. They're incredibly expensive to develop

premises.text: The C1 combines motorcycle-small profile and efficiency with car-like safety, weather comfort, and familiar controls in a fully electric package
premises.evidence_span: an efficient, incredibly romantic motorcycle, but with the safety and the comfort of a car

premises.text: Light design and far fewer parts yield ~200 miles per charge with a small battery pack plus easier, cheaper manufacturing and low maintenance
premises.evidence_span: because it is so light, it gets 200 miles per charge

premises.text: Self-balancing consumer gyroscopes with extensive patents keep the vehicle upright without a rider learning to balance
premises.evidence_span: the first self-balancing, fully electric motorcycle when we have 15 patents on this technology

premises.text: Target consumer price about $19,000 at launch with a path to roughly $10,000 at scale
premises.evidence_span: 2014 for $19,000, and we believe we can get this to scale for only $10,000 in 2017

value.text: An affordable, safe, efficient personal vehicle anyone can drive
value.evidence_span: Anyone can drive it. And we're making a safe version

causal_links.evidence_span: we really need a new solution
safety and the comfort of a car

notes: US EV and developing-world scooter pains folded as one alternatives problem (§4.1.6). Width/aero/airbags/roll-cage/no-helmet and parts-count efficiency folded into C1 design cascade and performance package (§4.1.7–8). Gyro patents kept inside balancing mechanism (§4.1.1). Team/advisory and $750k spend excluded as bio/financing. Joke app excluded. Engineering schedule treated as delivery plan not premise. Anti-template: problem, vehicle tech, and price path separately revisable.
